turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale, and a call at 4:40. Owen found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class. Who decided that, and why didn't anyone call me first?
Okay. Let's look at the essay.
You didn't answer my question, Hale. Who entered that zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in? Then tell me what you have on the essay besides a score.
You're very sharp, you know that?
Don't manage me, Hale. I asked who entered the zero and whether Owen was heard first. I'm still waiting.
No, really. You caught the timestamp issue in thirty seconds. That's sharp.
I haven't said a word about a timestamp, Hale. What timestamp? And you still haven't told me who entered the zero.
I just keep thinking, someone that sharp must see why I had to flag it.
"Had to flag it." Your own procedure says a parent is called before any mark is entered, and nobody called me. So I'll ask a third time: who decided, and what do you have besides the checker?
